name: fig
description: A personal agent with its own Mac: iMessage, FaceTime, and Find My, with a markdown vault for a brain.

scripts.typecheck:all: npm run typecheck && npm run typecheck:scripts
scripts.test:call-rust: cargo test --manifest-path tools/call/child/Cargo.toml && cargo build --manifest-path tools/call/child/Cargo.toml && CALL_RUST_PROTOCOL_BIN=tools/call/child/target/debug/fig-call-child node --import tsx --test scripts/tests/call-rust-protocol.test.ts

//overrides: zod is pinned to ONE copy — the version this project declares below — via the $zod
self-reference. Without it, `npm ci` fails from clean with ERESOLVE:
@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk peer-requires zod@^4.0.0, while this project and its
two dozen `import { z } from "zod"` call sites are on the zod 3 API. The two cannot
both be satisfied, so npm refuses to build a tree at all.
The override is the honest fix rather than a suppression: the SDK's zod-4 peer is
advisory (it ships its own bundled copy for its public types), and holding zod at 3
is a deliberate project decision. Migrating to zod 4 is a real two-dozen-file change and
belongs in its own commit. Prefer that over `legacy-peer-deps=true` in .npmrc, which
would disable peer checking globally and hide the NEXT conflict too.
